answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with earned, decaying reputation tied to verifiable work. Like a cedar that grows slowly, each identity gains influence only after completing attested, useful tasks over time, with its weight capped and recorded by a quill of public audit logs. New identities start near a low knoll of trust and cannot vote or mine at full power. Reputation decays without continued honest work, so an attacker must pay real computation and time for every fake identity, making mass forgery expensive while a single honest agent stays cheap.
